al-Qasimi, *Mahasin al-Ta'wil*, on Surah 66, verse 1:

Surah al-Tahrim

It is Medinan, and its number of verses is twelve.

In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[1] ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

al-Mahayimi said: He addressed him so that he would turn wholly towards Him and turn away from everything else, including the wives and others. He referred to him by the ambiguous term (ayyuha), indicating that this is due to his extreme greatness, such that his true reality cannot be known. He used the word "the Prophet" to indicate that he is the one who was informed of the secrets of Divine permission and prohibition. The meaning of his "forbidding" what was lawful for him is that he refrained from it and prohibited it for himself. This degree is permissible, and there is no sin in committing it. He was only told, ﴿Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ out of gentleness towards him, compassion for him, and to honour his rank and station, ﷺ, that he should attend to the approval of his wives by means of something that burdens him. This accords with the kindness Allah the Exalted had long shown to His Prophet, and with His raising him above being distressed on account of any of the human beings who are his followers, and for whose sake they were created, so that Allah might display the perfection of his prophethood through the manifestation of their deficiency compared to him, as al-Nasir has stated.

Two points:

The first: Concerning that which he, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, forbade for himself, the traditionists (al-Athariyyun, the adherents of transmitted reports) have narrations:

al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh and would stay with her. So I and Hafsa agreed that whichever of us he entered upon, she would say to him: 'I smell from you the odour of maghafir (a sweet resin with a foul smell). Have you eaten maghafir?' He entered upon one of us and she said that to him, and he said: 'Rather, I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will not return to it, and I have sworn! Do not tell anyone about this.' Then the verse was revealed."

al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated from Aisha that the Prophet ﷺ loved sweets and honey, and that when he had prayed the 'Asr he would go round his wives, drawing near to each of them. He entered upon Hafsa bint Umar and stayed with her longer than he usually did. I asked about that and was told: "A woman of her people had sent her a jar of honey, and she gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a drink of it." I said: "By Allah, we shall devise a plan against him!" I mentioned that to Sawda and said to her: "When he enters upon you and comes close to you, say to him: 'O Messenger of Allah! Have you eaten maghafir?' He will say to you: 'No!' Then say to him: 'What is this smell?' For he ﷺ disliked that an offensive odour should be found on him. He will say to you: 'Hafsa gave me a drink of honey.' Then say to him: 'Its bees have eaten the 'urfut (a tree), until the honey took on that offensive smell.'" [Aisha continued:] "When he enters upon me I will say that to him, and you, O Safiyya, say that too." When he entered upon Sawda, she said to him what Aisha had taught her, and he answered her with what had already been mentioned. When he entered upon Safiyya, she said the same to him. When he entered upon Aisha, she said the same to him. Then the next day, when he entered upon Hafsa, she said to him: "O Messenger of Allah! Shall I not give you some of it to drink?" He said: "I have no need of it." She said: "Sawda says: 'Glory be to Allah! We have deprived him of it!'" I said to her: "Be quiet."

Maghafir is a sweet gum with a foul odour, exuded by a tree called al-'Urfut, with the 'ayn pointed (ʿurfuṭ) and the fa vowelled.

In this narration, the woman at whose house he drank the honey was Hafsa, whereas in the previous one it was Zaynab. The confusion over the name does no harm, once the basic account of the incident is established.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Hafsa and Aisha were close friends, and both were wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Hafsa went to her father and sat talking with him. The Prophet ﷺ sent for his slave-girl, and she remained with him in Hafsa's house, on the day when he was due to be with Aisha. Hafsa returned, found her in her house, and began waiting for her to come out, and she was overcome by a very intense jealousy. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had his slave-girl brought out, and Hafsa entered and said: 'I have seen who was with you! By Allah, you have hurt me!' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By Allah, I will make you content, for I will tell you a secret, so keep it safe!' She said: 'What is it?' He said: 'I call you to witness that this slave-girl of mine is forbidden to me, to please you.'" (Hafsa and Aisha had been backing each other against the other wives of the Prophet ﷺ.) "Then Aisha went off and confided to her: 'Rejoice, for the Prophet ﷺ has forbidden his slave-girl to himself.' When she informed of the secret of the Prophet ﷺ, Allah the Mighty and Majestic made the Prophet ﷺ known to it, and Allah sent down to His Messenger, because the two had backed each other against him: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ and the verses that follow."

It is also narrated from al-Dahhak, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a slave-girl with whom he had intercourse. Hafsa saw him with her, and it was Aisha's day, and the two were backing each other. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Keep it secret for me, and do not mention to Aisha what you have seen.' Hafsa told Aisha, and Aisha became angry. She continued to press the Prophet of Allah ﷺ until he swore that he would never go near her again. So Allah revealed this verse, and commanded him to make expiation for his oath and to go to his slave-girl."

al-Nasa'i narrated from Anas that the Prophet ﷺ had a slave-girl with whom he had intercourse, and Hafsa and Aisha kept at him until he forbade her to himself, so Allah revealed this verse.

Ibn Jarir did not prefer one of the two reported causes of revelation over the other. Rather, he stopped at the general sense of the verse, as is his habit with such passages. For this reason he said: "The correct position is to say: what the Prophet ﷺ forbade to himself was something Allah had made lawful for him. It is possible that it was his slave-girl, possible that it was a certain drink, and possible that it was something else. But whatever it was, it was the prohibition of a thing that had been lawful for him. So Allah rebuked him for forbidding it to himself, just as it had been made lawful for him, and He showed him the release of his oath." End of quotation.

What appears to me is to prefer the reports that the forbidden thing was the slave-girl, as the cause of revelation, for several reasons:

Among them: such a person would seek by it the approval of the co-wives, and would take care of this on their behalf.

Among them: the reports about drinking honey do not indicate that he forbade it in order to seek their approval. Rather, they state that he swore not to drink it out of distaste for its smell, then asked Aisha not to tell his co-wife about it out of compassion for her. Unless the wives had reproached him for it, his noble temperament would not have tolerated that, and so he forbade it. But there is nothing in the narration that suggests this. Anything beyond that comes from the reporters' own reasoning.

Among them: the concern with revealing a separate surah was to rebuke and discipline his wives, ﷺ, for backing one another against him, to warn them against persisting in this, by citing them as evidence, and to inform them of the exalted rank of his station, and that his supporters are Allah his Protector, Gabriel, the angels, and the believers. All of this indicates that a great matter had driven them to forbid what he forbade, and this was nothing but jealousy, of the kind reported concerning the slave-girl. For wives are most eager to cut off whatever severs the bond of the weaker co-wife and removes her from the body of marriage. This is what has become clear to me so far.

As for the attribution of the honey report to this verse, and the statement of some of the early scholars (al-Salaf) that it was revealed concerning it, what is meant is that the verse includes his story in its general wording, as is known from the custom of the early scholars when they say: "It was revealed concerning such and such," as we have pointed out repeatedly. It seems that he, peace be upon him, had forbidden that drink, and then the narrators informed that for such a case an expiation for the oath (tahillah, the release from the oath) was prescribed, so there is no obstacle to returning to drinking it. And Allah knows best.

The second: In al-Iklil (a work of Qur'anic exegesis), it is used as evidence that whoever forbids to himself a slave-girl, food, or a wife, that thing does not become unlawful for him, and he is obliged to make the expiation for an oath.

al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said, concerning the one who declares something unlawful: he must make expiation. "Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah there is for you a good example."

Ibn Jarir held that the prohibition was accompanied by an oath, and he rejected the idea that prohibition by itself constitutes an oath. This is open to question, because in their usage the word "oath" (yamin) is more general than swearing by Allah. This was the view of Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ibn Jubayr, and others.

Qatadah said: "The Prophet ﷺ forbade her, meaning his slave-girl, so it became an oath." Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Something that supports this will come later. And the saying of Allah the Exalted:

**The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[2] ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths. And Allah is your Protector, and He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.﴾

﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾: that is, He has prescribed their dissolution (*tahlil*), which is the undoing of what you have bound, by means of the expiation (*kaffarah*, the atonement for breaking an oath). *Tahillah* is a verbal noun meaning *tahlil* (dissolution).

﴿And Allah is your Protector﴾: that is, the One who manages your affairs. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾: of your welfare. ﴿The All-Wise﴾: in His governance of you through what He has legislated and decreed.

**Notes:**

**First:** Ibn Qudamah said in *al-Rawdah* (*Rawdat al-Nazir*, on the principles of jurisprudence): The verse indicates that the ruling of His address to the Prophet (ﷺ) is not restricted to him. For when He rebuked him for prohibiting what Allah had made lawful to him, He said immediately after it: ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾, and He began the address by calling him alone, then completed it with the plural form by saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]. The question is lengthy in the principles of jurisprudence (*usul al-fiqh*).

[p-٥٨٥٧]

**Second:** Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah said: *Tahillah* is the verbal noun of *hallaltu al-shay'a tahlilan wa tahillatan* (I dissolved the thing), just as one says *karramtuhu takriman wa takrimah* (I honored him). This verbal noun may also be used to designate the dissolver itself, which is the expiation. If the verbal noun is intended, the meaning is: Allah has ordained for you the dissolution of the oath, which is its undoing, the opposite of binding. For this reason, those among our companions and others who held this view, such as Abu Bakr 'Abd al-'Aziz, used this verse as evidence for expiating before breaking an oath. This is because the dissolution cannot occur after the breaking, since by breaking the oath it is already dissolved. The dissolution occurs only when it is paid before the breaking, so that the oath may be dissolved. After the breaking, it is an expiation (*kaffarah*), because it atones for the sin entailed in breaking the covenant of Allah. When it becomes clear that what an oath requires is the obligation to fulfil it, Allah lifted this from this community through the expiation which He made a substitute for fulfilment, among the things He lifted from them of the heavy burdens (*asar*).

**Third:** His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿your oaths﴾ includes the prohibition of the lawful thing mentioned before it, which is the wife, since it enters into it by primary inclusion, and indeed every oath.

Taqi al-Din Ibn Taymiyyah said in his *Fatawa*: His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ is a general text concerning every oath that Muslims swear: that Allah has ordained a dissolution for it. He mentioned it, glorified is He, in the plural address to the community after the singular address to the Prophet (ﷺ), while He, glorified is He, knows that the community swears by various oaths. So if one oath were assumed to have no dissolution, that would contradict the verse. How much more so, since this is a general text in which no single instance has been specified, neither by text nor by consensus (*ijma'*). Rather, it is general in meaning as well as in its wording. For an oath is a binding that obliges the responsible person to refrain from an action, so the legislating of a dissolution for this binding is fitting, given what it contains of lightening and ease. This is found more in oaths of divorce and emancipation than in other oaths, such as the vows of contention and anger (*nadhr al-lajaj wal-ghadab*). For if a man swears by divorce that he will kill a soul, or that he will sever his kinship ties, or that he will withhold what is obligatory upon him, such as the discharge of a trust or the like, he makes divorce a stake for his oath, [p-٥٨٥٨] so that he may fulfil it and reconcile people, more than he would make Allah a stake. Then if he keeps his oath, there is upon him harm to this world and to religion, the entry into which the Muslims have unanimously agreed is prohibited. And if he divorces his wife, then in divorce too there is harm to this world and to religion, the entry into which the Muslims have unanimously agreed is prohibited. Moreover, He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1]. This implies that there is no prohibition of what Allah has made lawful except that Allah is Forgiving to its doer and Merciful to him, and that there is no cause that necessitates the establishment of the prohibition. For His saying "why" is an interrogation carrying the meaning of negation and denial; the implied sense is: there is no cause for your prohibiting what Allah has made lawful for you, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. So if the one who swears by a vow, emancipation or divorce were to intend not to do something for which there is no dispensation, there would be a cause requiring the prohibition of the lawful, and the requirement of forgiveness and mercy would not remain for this doer.

What further clarifies its generality is that they included the oath of divorce within the general scope of the hadith: "Whoever swears and says, 'If Allah wills,' then if He wills he does it, and if He wills he leaves it." They included in it the oath of divorce, emancipation, vows, and oaths by Allah. This indication is a reminder of the principles of al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and whoever agrees with them on the question of the vow of contention and anger. For they argued for expiation in it by this verse, and they made His saying ﴿the dissolution of your oaths﴾ — the expiation of your oaths — general to the oath by Allah and the oath by a vow. It is known that the inclusion of the wording of the vow of contention and anger, in pilgrimage, emancipation and the like, is equal.

If it is said: The verse means only the oath by Allah, for this is what is understood from the unrestricted term "oath," and the definite article and the annexation in His saying ﴿you have bound the oaths﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89] and ﴿the dissolution of your oaths﴾ may refer to the oath known to them, which is the oath by Allah. In that case, nothing is understood from the wording [p-٥٨٥٩] except what is familiar to them, and swearing by divorce or the like was not familiar to them. Even if the wording is general, we know that the oath which is not legislated does not enter into it, such as oaths by created things. So swearing by divorce or the like does not enter, since it is not a legislated oath, given His saying: "Whoever is swearing, let him swear by Allah, or else let him keep silent." This is the question of one who says: Every oath that is not legislated has no expiation for it and no breaking.

It is said: The term "oath" includes all of this, by the evidence of the usage of the Prophet (ﷺ), the Companions and the scholars of the term "oath" for all of this. Such as His saying (ﷺ): "The vow is an oath." And the Companions' saying to one who swore by an offering or emancipation: "Expiate your oath." Thus the Companions understood it from the words of the Prophet (ﷺ), and scholars included it in his saying (ﷺ): "Whoever swears and says, 'If Allah wills,' then if He wills he does it, and if He wills he leaves it." What indicates its generality in the verse is that He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1], then said: ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. This implies that the very act of prohibiting the lawful is an oath, as Ibn 'Abbas argued from it. The cause of the revelation of the verse is either his prohibiting honey, or his prohibiting Maria the Copt. On either account, the prohibition of the lawful is an oath according to the apparent meaning of the verse, though it is not an oath by Allah. For this reason, the majority of the Companions, such as 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas and others, gave the ruling that the prohibition of the lawful is an oath requiring expiation, either a major expiation like that for *zihar* (the pre-Islamic repudiation of a wife), or a minor expiation like that for an oath by Allah. The early generations continued to call *zihar* and the like an oath.

Also, His saying ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1] either means: why do you prohibit it by the wording of "prohibition," or: why do you prohibit it by an oath by Allah, Exalted is He, or the like, or: why do you prohibit it in general. If the first and third are intended, then its prohibition is established by means other than an oath by Allah, Exalted is He, and so the ruling is general. If it is intended to mean prohibiting it by an oath by Allah, then Allah has named the oath by Allah a prohibition of the lawful. It is known that the oath by Allah does not make the legal prohibition obligatory, but since it obliges the one who swears to refrain from the act, it has forbidden him the act, so it enters into the force of His saying: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1]. Then His saying ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ must encompass every oath that prohibits the lawful, for this is the ruling of that act, so it must correspond to its forms. For the prohibition of the lawful is the cause of His saying ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾, and when the cause of an answer is general, the answer is general, so that it does not become an answer concerning some but not others, given the presence of the cause that requires generalization.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Zad al-Ma'ad*: Those who obligated the expiation of an oath for prohibition are more closely aligned with the text than those who dropped it. For Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the dissolution of oaths immediately after His saying ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1], and this is explicit that the prohibition of the lawful has had the dissolution of oaths ordained for it, whether specific to it or inclusive of it and others. So it is not permissible for the cause of the expiation mentioned in the context to be left without the ruling of expiation and to be linked to something else, and this is clearly impermissible.

Furthermore, forbidding oneself an act by prohibition is like forbidding it by oath, indeed stronger. For if an oath involves violating the sanctity of His name, glorified is He, then prohibition involves violating the sanctity of His law and command. For when He legislates something lawful and the responsible person prohibits it, his prohibition is a violation of the sanctity of what He legislated.

We say: Breaking an oath does not involve violating the sanctity of the Name, nor does prohibition involve violating the sanctity of the Law, as some jurists claim. This is a very corrupt reason. For breaking an oath is either permissible, obligatory, or recommended. Allah never permitted anyone to violate the sanctity of His name at all, yet He legislated for His servants the breaking of an oath together with expiation. The Prophet (ﷺ) informed that if one swears to an oath and sees something other than it as better, he expiates his oath and does the thing sworn about. [p-٥٨٦١] It is known that violating the sanctity of His name, blessed and exalted is He, has never been permitted in any law. Rather, the expiation, as Allah, Exalted is He, named it, is a *tahillah* (dissolution), which is a *taf'ilah* from *hill* (lawfulness): it dissolves only what the oath has bound. This binding, just as it occurs through oath, occurs through prohibition. The secret of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Allah has certainly ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾ becomes clear when placed after His saying ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1].

He, may Allah have mercy on him, also said about this earlier: As for one who says that it is an oath requiring expiation in every case, his basis is that prohibiting the lawful, such as food, drink and clothing, is an oath which is expiated by the text, the meaning, and the reports of the Companions. For Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1], and so on. It must be that the prohibition of the lawful falls under this ordinance, since it is its cause. Restricting the locus of the cause from the general statement is absolutely impermissible, for it is the principal object of explanation. If it were restricted, the cause of the ruling would be left without explanation, and this is impermissible. This is an argument of the utmost strength. So I asked Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, about it, and he said: Yes! The prohibition is a major oath regarding the wife, whose expiation is the expiation of *zihar*, and a minor oath regarding other things, whose expiation is the expiation of an oath by Allah. He said: This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and others among the Companions and those after them: that the prohibition is an oath which is expiated.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, also said in *A'lam al-Muwaqqi'in*: It is not permissible to separate a Muslim from his wife by a wording not established for divorce, nor intended as divorce. He is liable for the expiation of an oath concerning his forbidden relation, due to the severity of the oath, since it is not like swearing by a created thing, which is not binding, nor is it a mere slip of oath. Rather it is a binding oath, and so there is in it the expiation of an oath.

Then he said, regarding the thirteenth position: it is an oath, and the expiation that atones for an oath atones for it in every case. This view is also reported as sound from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Mas'ud, Abdullah ibn Umar, Ikrimah, Ata', Makhul, Qatadah, al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Jabir ibn Zayd, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Nafi', al-Awza'i, and Abu Thawr, and others besides them, may Allah be pleased with them all. The proof for this view is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the prescription of the dissolution of oaths immediately after the prohibition of what is lawful, so it must necessarily apply to it with certainty, and it is not permissible to make the dissolution of oaths apply to something other than what was mentioned before it, and the thing mentioned is thereby excluded from the ruling of the dissolution for which its mention was intended.

In Zad al-Ma'ad he said: There is no difference, according to the majority of scholars, between the prohibition (of something) other than a wife, whether it concerns a slave-girl or anything else, except al-Shafi'i alone; for he required the expiation of an oath specifically in the prohibition of a slave-girl, since prohibition has an effect on intimate relations according to him, but not on other things. Furthermore, the occasion of revelation of the verse was the prohibition of a slave-girl, and the locus of the occasion of revelation cannot be excluded from the ruling, while the ruling also applies to other things. His opponents say: the text linked the obligation of dissolving the oath to the prohibition of what is lawful, and this is more general than the prohibition of a slave-girl and other things, so expiation is obligatory wherever its cause is found. This has already been explained.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He:

[3] ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement. And when she informed [another wife] of it, and Allah made it known to him, he made known part of it and ignored part. And when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "The All-Knowing, All-Aware informed me."﴾.

﴿And when the Prophet﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿confided to one of his wives a statement﴾ is Hafsah, according to the narrators Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son 'Abd al-Rahman, al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari). ﴿A statement﴾ is, in their view, his declaring forbidden his concubine (Mariyah). Ibn Jarir said: "Or [it is] what he forbade for himself of that which Allah, may His praise be exalted, had made lawful for him." And His saying: "«Do not mention that to anyone.»"

﴿And when she informed [another wife] of it﴾ means she told the secret to her companion, as mentioned earlier. ﴿And Allah made it known to him﴾ means He informed him of her telling of it. ﴿He made known part of it﴾ means he informed her of part of what she had spread, rebuking her. ﴿And ignored part﴾ (p-5863) means part of the statement, out of generosity. ﴿And when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "The All-Knowing, All-Aware informed me."﴾ meaning the One from whom nothing is hidden.

Note (tanbih): In "al-Iklil" it is said that the verse shows there is no harm in confiding part of a statement to one who is relied upon, whether a wife or a friend, and that the one so trusted is obliged to keep it secret. It also shows good companionship with wives, gentleness in rebuke, and overlooking the scrutiny of a fault.

Al-Zamakhshari related from Sufyan that he said: "Overlooking has never ceased to be the practice of the noble."

Then Allah, exalted be He, pointed to His anger on behalf of His Prophet, may Allah's blessings be upon him, at what she did by spreading the secret to her companion, and at their both backing each other against what troubled his peace, and that this is a sin for which repentance is required, through His saying, glorified be He:

**The explanation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[4] ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined [toward the truth]; but if you back one another against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are [his] supporters.﴾

﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ means: toward the truth, which is what is obligatory, namely keeping away from what angers His Messenger. It is authentically related from Ibn 'Abbas that he asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, about the two women who had banded together against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'A'isha and Hafsa.

In their address, there is an emphasis through the shift (al-iltifat, the grammatical turn from the third person to the second person). The one who is intensely reproaching makes the one being reproached seem cast out and distant from the presence, and then, when his anger intensifies, he turns toward him and reproaches him with whatever he wishes.

﴿But if you back one another against him﴾ means: if you band together and agree upon what distresses him, ﴿then indeed Allah is his protector, and Gabriel and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after that are [his] supporters﴾ (p-5864), meaning they support one another against whoever intends to harm him. So what good is the backing of two women against one whose supporters are these? And since the angels are the greatest and most numerous of the created beings, He concluded the list of supporters with them, so that it would be more magnificent in honouring the Prophet, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, in exalting his station, and in giving him victory. For they here are like a mighty army filling the deserts, whose commander and leader is moved to attack his enemy and opponent.

The Interpretation of His Words, may He be exalted:

[5] ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you: submitting (muslimat), believing (mu'minat), obedient (qanitat), repentant (ta'ibat), worshipping ('abidat), travelling (sa'ihat), previously married (thayyibat) and virgins (abkaran).﴾

﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him in exchange wives better than you: muslimat﴾ i.e., submitting to God in obedience. ﴿mu'minat﴾ i.e., affirming belief in God and His Messenger. ﴿qanitat﴾ i.e., obedient to what they are commanded. ﴿ta'ibat﴾ i.e., repentant of sins, not persisting in them. ﴿'abidat﴾ i.e., devoted in worship to God, as if worship had mingled with their hearts until it became a disposition (malakah) in them. ﴿sa'ihat﴾ It was said: its meaning is fasting women, and we will draw attention to what is in this view. ﴿thayyibat wa-abkaran﴾

Know that in describing the replacement wives with these attributes there is an implicit hint that wives must possess them, especially the wives of the Prophet ﷺ.

Note:

Many exegetes held that what is meant by ﴿sa'ihat﴾ is fasting women or emigrating women. We have already stated, in the commentary on Surah al-Tawbah regarding ﴿al-sa'ihun﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112], that the correct view there is the literal meaning, since nothing prevents it, and one does not turn to the figurative meaning except for a reason that prevents the literal. Hence some verifying scholars said: this verse indicates that travel (siyahah) is permitted for women, just as it is for men. Thus the meaning of His words, may He be exalted, ﴿sa'ihat﴾ is travelling women, whether the travel is for emigration or for observing the traces of the vanished nations. The Sunnah has specified the general scope of their travel by making it accompanied by a husband or a mahram of theirs, for their protection.

(p-5865) Then he said: It seems that what prompted some to interpret ﴿sa'ihat﴾ as fasting women, or specifically emigrating women, is their imagining that travelling in lands does not suit the nature of women who are commanded to observe hijab. It is as if he understands from hijab that it is perpetual confinement, or as if fresh air were a blessing specific to other than women, or as if they were created only for the prisons of houses, which may be harsher than the deepest prisons of criminals, or as if no part of this vast world were made for them except a single house?! As for His words, may He be exalted: ﴿He created for you all that is in the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], it seems to be restricted to men, or as if the verses commanding travel for contemplation, lesson, comprehension and experience were sent down from heaven not for the whole community, but for half of it, namely men. Far be that! Where is his guidance ﷺ in travelling with his wives? For he ««used to draw lots among them, and whichever of them the lot came out for, he took her out with him, and she travelled with him»». This became an established law practised in the religion. Likewise it is authentically reported that he ﷺ ««when he arrived with Safiyyah, seated her behind him, while he was with the caravan»».

In sum, travel in the noble Qur'an does not aim at one single end, but at several ends and benefits:

First: The apprehension of intellectual matters and the comprehension of the lessons of what is heard, as we learn from the verse: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth, so that they have hearts with which to understand or ears with which to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that are blind, but the hearts within the breasts that are blind﴾ [al-Hajj: 46].

Second: Acquaintance with the conditions of the vanished nations and the grand traces they left, which call for reflection, as we learn from the words of the Wise Book: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in traces upon the earth, but God seized them for their sins, and they had no protector from God﴾ [Ghafir: 21].

(p-5866) And His words: ﴿Have they not travelled in the earth and seen how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength, and they ploughed the earth and built it up more than they built it, and their messengers came to them with clear proofs. God was not to wrong them, but they were wronging themselves﴾ [al-Rum: 9].

Third: Searching and investigating the regions of the inhabited world by looking at the cosmos and at the various arts, in order to reach knowledge of the Originator of this world, exalted is He, as the noble Book urges us to ascend this lofty height by His words: ﴿Say: Travel in the earth and see how He originated creation﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 20].

Fourth: Gaining the profit of trade, as we learn from the words of the noble Book: ﴿And others travel in the earth seeking of God's bounty﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20].

Do you see these significant benefits as restricted to men to the exclusion of women, so that travel is specific to men? Certainly not! God has bestowed favour upon the people of Sheba with what He related in His words: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed other visible towns, and We determined therein the stages of travel: travel therein by night and by day in security﴾ [Saba': 18]. And He bestowed favour upon all His servants by His words: ﴿It is He who enables you to travel on land and sea﴾ [Yunus: 22]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿A provision for you and for the travellers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96]. So is it permissible to say that these favours are among the special privileges of men to the exclusion of women? Certainly not! Rather all are covered by these favours, as the general scope of the verses requires. End, summarised.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: [6] ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones; over it are angels, stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ means: its cause, which is by abandoning sins (p-٥٨٦٧) and performing acts of obedience, and by standing over the discipline of the family and holding them to the same standards you hold yourselves. ﴿Whose fuel is men and stones﴾ means: it blazes with them, just as other fires blaze with firewood. ﴿Over it are angels﴾ means: they are in charge of its affairs and of punishing its people, the Zabaniyah (the guardians of Hell). ﴿Stern and severe﴾ means: harsh and hard-hearted. ﴿Who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: the two clauses do not have the same meaning. The meaning of the first is that they accept His commands, adhere to them, and neither refuse nor reject them. The meaning of the second is that they carry out what they are commanded, without being sluggish about it or negligent in it. (End of quotation.)

It has also been said: the first clause explains the continuity of their carrying out His commands, and the second explains that they do nothing unless they have been commanded to do it, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿while they act by His command﴾ [al-Anbiya: 27]. Their continual doing of what they are commanded is what conveys this, so there is no repetition. It has also been said that this is from al-tard wa al-'aks (the method of converse inference, in which the meaning of one of two statements confirms the implied meaning of the other, and vice versa), which occurs across two statements, where the stated meaning of one establishes the implied meaning of the other, and the reverse.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ That is: it will be said to them this when they enter the Fire. So what is meant by ﴿today﴾ is the time of their entering it, and its definiteness is for a known reference (al-ʿahd), and the prohibition of making excuses is because there is no excuse for them, or because the excuse will not benefit them.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[8] ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will run before them and on their right. They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent."﴾ (p-5868)

﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾ That is: a repentance that mends the tears, stitches up the rips, repairs what is corrupt, and fills the gap. It derives from *nasḥ* (sewing, stitching). Or it means a repentance purified of any admixture of inclination toward the state from which one repented, of looking back at it, and of regarding it with no turning toward it and cutting off all regard for it. It derives from *al-naṣūḥ* in the sense of purity (*al-khulūṣ*).

﴿Perhaps your Lord﴾ That is: by advising your souls with sincere repentance.

﴿will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him﴾ That is: He will not humiliate them. It is an allusion to their enemies being subjected to disgrace and abasement.

﴿Their light will run before them and on their right. They will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light﴾ That is: sustain it or increase it.

﴿and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 66, verse 9:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾

﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, i.e., with the sword (al-sinan) and with proof (al-burhan). ﴿And be stern with them﴾, i.e., in what you strive against them with, so that their firmness is broken, their obstinacy (shakimah) and disposition (ʿarikah) are softened, and their souls are subdued, humbled and made submissive.

﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so those two could not avail them anything against God. And it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾

(p. 5869) ﴿God presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾, that is, their condition. ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them﴾, that is, by supporting others against them, by disbelief and disobedience, although they were able to obey and believe. ﴿So those two could not avail them against God﴾, that is, against His punishment, ﴿anything. And it was said﴾, that is, to them at the time of their death, or on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿"Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ That is, with the rest of those who enter, the wicked who have no connection between them and the prophets.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 66, verses 11–12:**

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[11–12] ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people." And Mary, daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our spirit, and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devoutly obedient.﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12]

﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is: from their deeds and their punishment.

﴿And Mary, daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12], that is, she preserved it and protected it.

﴿So We breathed into it of Our spirit﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12]: this means Jibril, peace be upon him; or "of a spirit," which We created without intermediary, and that is ʿIsa, peace be upon him.

﴿And she believed in the words of her Lord﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12]: that is, in His revealed scrolls sent down from Him. ﴿And His scriptures﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12]: that is, the inspired ones. The conjunction (al-ʿatf) is for explanation, or "the words" (al-kalimat) is more general than the written and the memorised commands and enjoined precepts passed down, while "the scriptures" (al-kutub) is specific to the written books.

﴿And she was among the devoutly obedient﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12]: that is, among those who persistently adhere to obedience to Allah and submit to His rulings. The masculine form (al-tadhkir) of al-qanitin is used for taghlib (the predominance of the masculine gender in grammar).

**Remarks:**

**First:** Al-Zamakhshari said: Allah, mighty and majestic, has made the example of the disbelievers, in that they are punished for their disbelief [p. 5870] and their enmity toward the believers, the punishment of their like, without leniency, favour, or partiality. Their kinship or ties by marriage with the believers do not benefit them, given their enmity toward them, because their enmity toward them and their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger sever the bonds, cut off connection, and make them further than strangers. Even if the believer to whom the disbeliever is connected is a prophet of Allah's prophets, the example is the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot. When they were hypocritical and betrayed the two Messengers, the two Messengers did not avail them against the punishment of Allah at all, despite the bond of marriage between them. And He presented the example of the believers: the connection of disbelievers does not harm them, nor does it diminish any of their reward or their nearness to Allah, by the example of the wife of Pharaoh and her station with Allah, the Exalted, though she was the wife of the greatest enemy of Allah, who spoke the greatest word. And Mary, daughter of ʿImran, and what she was granted of the honour of this world and the Hereafter and the choosing above the women of the worlds, though her people were disbelievers. Within these two examples is an allusion (taʿrid) to the two mothers of the believers mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and to what proceeded from them of backing one another against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in a way he disliked. It is also a warning to them both in the strongest and most severe manner, because the example includes mention of disbelief. Similar to this in severity is His words: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need of the worlds﴾ [Ali ʿImran: 97]. It also indicates that it is their right to be sincere and perfect in it like these two believing women, and not to rely on the fact that they are wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for that merit benefits them only if they are sincere. The allusion to Hafsa is more probable, because the wife of Lot disclosed his secret, just as Hafsa disclosed the secret of the Messenger of Allah. The secrets and symbols of the revelation are in every chapter, extremely subtle and hidden, to a degree that is fine for the perception of the scholar and slips beyond his insight. End of quotation.

**Second:** Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Aʿlam al-Muwaqqiʿin*: These verses contain three examples: one example for the disbelievers, and two examples for the believers.

The example of the disbelievers includes that the disbeliever is punished for his disbelief and his enmity toward Allah, His Messenger, and His allies, and that what existed between him and the believers of bonds of kinship, ties by marriage, or any cause of connection does not benefit him, given his disbelief. All causes will be severed on the Day of Resurrection, except what was connected to Allah alone through His messengers. If kinship, marriage, or wedlock benefited without faith, the bond that existed between Noah and Lot and their wives would have benefited. When neither of them availed them anything against Allah, and it was said: ﴿Enter the Fire with those who enter﴾, the verse then cut off the hope of whoever commits disobedience to Allah, opposes His command, and hopes that the righteousness of another, whether near or distant, will benefit him, even if there was between them in this world the strongest connection. There is no connection beyond the connection of sonship, fatherhood, and spousal relation. Noah did not avail his son, nor Abraham his father, nor Noah and Lot their wives against Allah at all. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Your relatives and your children will not benefit you on the Day of Resurrection; He will separate between you﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 3]. He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾ [al-Infitar: 19]. He said: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will compensate for another soul﴾ [al-Baqarah: 48], and: ﴿And fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is true﴾ [Luqman: 33]. All of this is a refutation of the false hopes of the polytheists, that those they relied upon besides Allah, whether relatives, in-laws, spouses, or companions, would benefit them on the Day of Resurrection, or protect them from the punishment of Allah, or intercede for them with Allah. This is the root of the misguidance and polytheism of the children of Adam, and it is the polytheism that Allah does not forgive. It is what Allah sent all His messengers to nullify, and sent down all His books to abolish, and to fight and oppose its adherents.

As for the two examples for the believers: the first is the wife of Pharaoh. The point of the example is that the connection of the believer with the disbeliever does not harm him at all when he separates from him in his disbelief and his deeds. The disobedience of another does not harm the obedient believer at all in the Hereafter, even if he is harmed by it in this world through the punishment that befalls the people of the earth when they neglect the command of Allah, for it comes generally. The connection of the wife of Pharaoh to him did not harm her, though he was the greatest of disbelievers, and the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them, though they were Messengers of the Lord of the worlds.

The second example for the believers: Mary, who had no husband, neither believer nor disbeliever.

[p. 5872] He mentioned three categories of women: the disbelieving woman who has a connection to a righteous man; the righteous woman who has a connection to a disbelieving man; and the unmarried woman who has no connection between her and anyone. The first, her connection does not benefit her, and neither does its cause. The second, her connection and its cause do not harm her. The third, the absence of connection does not harm her at all.

Then, within these examples are wondrous secrets fitting the context of the surah. It was brought in mention of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and a warning against their backing one another against him, and that if they do not obey Allah and His Messenger and do not desire the Hereafter, their connection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will not benefit them, just as the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them. For this reason, in this surah he struck the example of the connection of marriage rather than kinship.

Yahya ibn Salam said: Allah struck the first example warning ʿAʾisha and Hafsa, then He struck for them the second example encouraging them to hold fast to obedience. In striking the example of the believers with Mary there is another consideration: the slander of the enemies of Allah, the Jews, against her, and their attributing to her and her son what Allah had absolved her of, did not harm her with Allah at all, though she was the greatest truthful one (al-siddiqah al-kubra), chosen above the women of the worlds. Therefore, the disparagement of the wicked and the corrupt does not harm the righteous man.

In this there is consolation for ʿAʾisha, mother of the believers, if the surah was revealed after the incident of the slander (al-ifk), and a reassurance of her soul regarding what the liars said, if it was before it. Likewise, in mentioning the example of the wives of Noah and Lot there is a warning to her and to Hafsa regarding what they had relied upon against the Prophet ﷺ. These examples thus contain the warning to them, the threat and encouragement to them toward obedience, monotheism, and consolation, and reassurance of the soul for whoever among them is harmed and falsely accused. The secrets of the revelation are above this and greater than it, especially the secrets of the examples, which none understands except the learned. End of quotation.

**Third:** Al-Qashani said: Allah has made clear that natural bonds and outward connections are not considered in matters of the Hereafter. Rather, true love and spiritual connections are the only effective ones. Outward connections, based on natural kinship, familiarity, and association, leave no trace after death and exist only in this world, as the two examples mentioned show. The consideration for deserving honour with Allah is righteous deeds and correct belief, like the chastity of Mary, her affirmation of the words of her Lord, and her obedience, which prepared her to receive the breathing of the spirit of Allah into her [p. 5873]. It may be suggested between them that the treacherous soul, which does not fulfil obedience, does not keep secrets, and permits opposition, is included in the fire of deprivation and the hell of separation together with those veiled, and the guidance of the spirit does not avail it anything in the matter of punishment. Also, the heart subdued under the domination of the Pharaonic commanding soul, which seeks deliverance by taking refuge in the Truth, in which the strength of Allah's love has grown strong because of its purity, and the strength of its subjugation of the self and Satan has weakened because of its weakness, does not remain in punishment by dwelling with it for long, and it suffers from its deeds for a little while. And the soul adorned with the virtue of chastity, indicated by "guarding the chastity," is the one receptive to the overflowing of the Holy Spirit, illuminated by the light of the Spirit, affirming the words of the Lord, from the wise doctrines and divine laws, obedient to Allah absolutely, in knowledge and action, secretly and openly. End of summary.

**Fourth:** In *al-Iklil*: It has been cited, by His words ﴿the wife of Pharaoh﴾, as evidence for the validity of the marriages of disbelievers. I say: It may also be cited by His words ﴿the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10] up to His words ﴿so they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10], as evidence for the permissibility of a righteous man continuing the marriage with his wicked, disobedient wife, and that retaining her without separation is not considered a lack of scrupulousness, which is clear. It may also be cited as evidence that marriage to polytheist women was permitted in the law of those before us, though Islam forbade it with the strongest prohibition, as has passed in many verses.

**Fifth:** Ibn Kathir said, regarding His words about the wife of Pharaoh: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾: The scholars said: she chose the neighbour before the dwelling. Something of this has been transmitted in a *marfuʿ* (traced to the Prophet) hadith.

**Sixth:** Al-Zamakhshari said: In the supplication of the wife of Pharaoh is evidence that seeking refuge in Allah, turning to Him, and asking for deliverance from Him at times of trial and calamity is among the practices of the righteous and the ways of the prophets and messengers: ﴿So decide between me and them with a decision, and deliver me and those with me of the believers﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 118]; ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾ [Yunus: 85]; ﴿And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾ [Yunus: 86].

All of this is a refutation of the false hopes of the polytheists, that those they relied upon besides Allah, whether relatives, in-laws, spouses, or companions, would benefit them on the Day of Resurrection, or protect them from the punishment of Allah, or intercede for them with Allah. This is the root of the misguidance and polytheism of the children of Adam, and it is the polytheism that Allah does not forgive. It is what Allah sent all His messengers to nullify, and sent down all His books to abolish, and to fight and oppose its adherents.

As for the two examples for the believers: the first is the wife of Pharaoh. The point of the example is that the connection of the believer with the disbeliever does not harm him at all when he separates from him in his disbelief and his deeds. The disobedience of another does not harm the obedient believer at all in the Hereafter, even if he is harmed by it in this world through the punishment that befalls the people of the earth when they neglect the command of Allah, for it comes generally. The connection of the wife of Pharaoh to him did not harm her, though he was the greatest of disbelievers, and the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them, though they were Messengers of the Lord of the worlds.

The second example for the believers: Mary, who had no husband, neither believer nor disbeliever.

[p. 5872] He mentioned three categories of women: the disbelieving woman who has a connection to a righteous man; the righteous woman who has a connection to a disbelieving man; and the unmarried woman who has no connection between her and anyone. The first, her connection does not benefit her, and neither does its cause. The second, her connection and its cause do not harm her. The third, the absence of connection does not harm her at all.

Then, within these examples are wondrous secrets fitting the context of the surah. It was brought in mention of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and a warning against their backing one another against him, and that if they do not obey Allah and His Messenger and do not desire the Hereafter, their connection to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will not benefit them, just as the connection of the wives of Noah and Lot to them did not benefit them. For this reason, in this surah he struck the example of the connection of marriage rather than kinship.

Yahya ibn Salam said: Allah struck the first example warning ʿAʾisha and Hafsa, then He struck for them the second example encouraging them to hold fast to obedience. In striking the example of the believers with Mary there is another consideration: the slander of the enemies of Allah, the Jews, against her, and their attributing to her and her son what Allah had absolved her of, did not harm her with Allah at all, though she was the greatest truthful one (al-siddiqah al-kubra), chosen above the women of the worlds. Therefore, the disparagement of the wicked and the corrupt does not harm the righteous man.

In this there is consolation for ʿAʾisha, mother of the believers, if the surah was revealed after the incident of the slander (al-ifk), and a reassurance of her soul regarding what the liars said, if it was before it. Likewise, in mentioning the example of the wives of Noah and Lot there is a warning to her and to Hafsa regarding what they had relied upon against the Prophet ﷺ. These examples thus contain the warning to them, the threat and encouragement to them toward obedience, monotheism, and consolation, and reassurance of the soul for whoever among them is harmed and falsely accused. The secrets of the revelation are above this and greater than it, especially the secrets of the examples, which none understands except the learned. End of quotation.

**Third:** Al-Qashani said: Allah has made clear that natural bonds and outward connections are not considered in matters of the Hereafter. Rather, true love and spiritual connections are the only effective ones. Outward connections, based on natural kinship, familiarity, and association, leave no trace after death and exist only in this world, as the two examples mentioned show. The consideration for deserving honour with Allah is righteous deeds and correct belief, like the chastity of Mary, her affirmation of the words of her Lord, and her obedience, which prepared her to receive the breathing of the spirit of Allah into her [p. 5873]. It may be suggested between them that the treacherous soul, which does not fulfil obedience, does not keep secrets, and permits opposition, is included in the fire of deprivation and the hell of separation together with those veiled, and the guidance of the spirit does not avail it anything in the matter of punishment. Also, the heart subdued under the domination of the Pharaonic commanding soul, which seeks deliverance by taking refuge in the Truth, in which the strength of Allah's love has grown strong because of its purity, and the strength of its subjugation of the self and Satan has weakened because of its weakness, does not remain in punishment by dwelling with it for long, and it suffers from its deeds for a little while. And the soul adorned with the virtue of chastity, indicated by "guarding the chastity," is the one receptive to the overflowing of the Holy Spirit, illuminated by the light of the Spirit, affirming the words of the Lord, from the wise doctrines and divine laws, obedient to Allah absolutely, in knowledge and action, secretly and openly. End of summary.

**Fourth:** In *al-Iklil*: It has been cited, by His words ﴿the wife of Pharaoh﴾, as evidence for the validity of the marriages of disbelievers. I say: It may also be cited by His words ﴿the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10] up to His words ﴿so they betrayed them both﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10], as evidence for the permissibility of a righteous man continuing the marriage with his wicked, disobedient wife, and that retaining her without separation is not considered a lack of scrupulousness, which is clear. It may also be cited as evidence that marriage to polytheist women was permitted in the law of those before us, though Islam forbade it with the strongest prohibition, as has passed in many verses.

**Fifth:** Ibn Kathir said, regarding His words about the wife of Pharaoh: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾: The scholars said: she chose the neighbour before the dwelling. Something of this has been transmitted in a *marfuʿ* (traced to the Prophet) hadith.

**Sixth:** Al-Zamakhshari said: In the supplication of the wife of Pharaoh is evidence that seeking refuge in Allah, turning to Him, and asking for deliverance from Him at times of trial and calamity is among the practices of the righteous and the ways of the prophets and messengers: ﴿So decide between me and them with a decision, and deliver me and those with me of the believers﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 118]; ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾ [Yunus: 85]; ﴿And deliver us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people﴾ [Yunus: 86].
